The number of solutions of \(\sqrt3\cos2\theta+8\cos\theta+3\sqrt3=0\), \(\theta\in[-3\pi,2\pi]\), is:

With \(\theta_0=\cos^{-1}\left(-\tfrac1{\sqrt3}\right)\in\left(\tfrac\pi2,\pi\right)\), the solutions in \([-3\pi,2\pi]\) are \(\theta_0,\ -\theta_0,\ 2\pi-\theta_0,\ \theta_0-2\pi,\ -2\pi-\theta_0\): \(5\) solutions.

Let \(\dfrac\pi2<\theta<\pi\) and \(\cot\theta=-\dfrac1{2\sqrt2}\). Then the value of \[\sin\left(\frac{15\theta}{2}\right)(\cos8\theta+\sin8\theta)+\cos\left(\frac{15\theta}{2}\right)(\cos8\theta-\sin8\theta)\] is equal to:
questions.sol:
Regrouping: \(\sin\left(\tfrac{15\theta}{2}-8\theta\right)+\cos\left(8\theta-\tfrac{15\theta}{2}\right)=\cos\tfrac\theta2-\sin\tfrac\theta2\).
\(\sin\theta=\tfrac{2\sqrt2}{3}\); \(\left(\cos\tfrac\theta2-\sin\tfrac\theta2\right)^2=1-\sin\theta=\tfrac{3-2\sqrt2}{3}\), and since \(\tfrac\theta2\in\left(\tfrac\pi4,\tfrac\pi2\right)\) the value is negative:
\(-\dfrac{\sqrt2-1}{\sqrt3}=\dfrac{1-\sqrt2}{\sqrt3}\).

If \(\cot x=\dfrac5{12}\) for some \(x\in\left(\pi,\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)\), then \[\sin7x\left(\cos\frac{13x}{2}+\sin\frac{13x}{2}\right)+\cos7x\left(\cos\frac{13x}{2}-\sin\frac{13x}{2}\right)\] is equal to:
questions.sol:
Regrouping: \(\sin\left(7x-\tfrac{13x}{2}\right)+\cos\left(7x-\tfrac{13x}{2}\right)=\sin\tfrac x2+\cos\tfrac x2\).
\(\sin x=-\tfrac{12}{13}\); \(\left(\sin\tfrac x2+\cos\tfrac x2\right)^2=1+\sin x=\tfrac1{13}\). For \(\tfrac x2\in\left(\tfrac\pi2,\tfrac{3\pi}4\right)\), \(\sin\tfrac x2>\left|\cos\tfrac x2\right|\), so the value is \(\tfrac1{\sqrt{13}}\).

questions.q: The number of elements in the set \(\{x\in[0,180^\circ]:\tan(x+100^\circ)=\tan(x+50^\circ)\tan x\tan(x-50^\circ)\}\) is ______.
questions.sol:
Write it as \(\dfrac{\tan(x+100^\circ)}{\tan x}=\tan(x+50^\circ)\tan(x-50^\circ)\), i.e.
\(\dfrac{\sin(2x+100^\circ)+\sin100^\circ}{\sin(2x+100^\circ)-\sin100^\circ}=\dfrac{\cos100^\circ-\cos2x}{\cos100^\circ+\cos2x}\).
Componendo–dividendo: \(\sin(2x+100^\circ)\cos2x=-\sin100^\circ\cos100^\circ\Rightarrow\sin(4x+100^\circ)=-(\sin100^\circ+\sin200^\circ)=-\cos50^\circ\).
With \(4x+100^\circ\in[100^\circ,820^\circ]\): \(4x+100^\circ=220^\circ,320^\circ,580^\circ,680^\circ\), i.e. \(x=30^\circ,55^\circ,120^\circ,145^\circ\) (all admissible). Answer: \(4\).

questions.q: If \(\dfrac{\tan(A-B)}{\tan A}+\dfrac{\sin^2C}{\sin^2A}=1\), \(A,B,C\in\left(0,\dfrac\pi2\right)\), then:
opts: \(\tan A,\tan B,\tan C\) are in G.P.
\(\tan A,\tan C,\tan B\) are in G.P.
\(\tan A,\tan B,\tan C\) are in A.P.
\(\tan A,\tan C,\tan B\) are in A.P.
questions.sol:
\(1-\dfrac{\tan(A-B)}{\tan A}=\dfrac{\sin A\cos(A-B)-\cos A\sin(A-B)}{\sin A\cos(A-B)}=\dfrac{\sin B}{\sin A\cos(A-B)}\).
So \(\sin^2C=\dfrac{\sin A\sin B}{\cos(A-B)}=\dfrac{\tan A\tan B}{1+\tan A\tan B}\). Since \(\sin^2C=\dfrac{\tan^2C}{1+\tan^2C}\), we get \(\tan^2C=\tan A\tan B\).

questions.q: If \(k=\tan\left(\dfrac\pi4+\dfrac12\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac23\right)\right)+\tan\left(\dfrac12\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac23\right)\right)\), then the number of solutions of the equation \(\sin^{-1}(kx-1)=\sin^{-1}x-\cos^{-1}x\) is ______.
questions.sol:
\(\tan\tfrac\theta2=\tfrac1{\sqrt5}\) for \(\cos\theta=\tfrac23\), so the first term is \(\dfrac{\sqrt5+1}{\sqrt5-1}=\dfrac{3+\sqrt5}{2}\); for \(\sin\phi=\tfrac23\), \(\tan\tfrac\phi2=\dfrac{2/3}{1+\sqrt5/3}=\dfrac{3-\sqrt5}{2}\). So \(k=3\).
RHS \(=2\sin^{-1}x-\tfrac\pi2\in\left[-\tfrac\pi2,\tfrac\pi2\right]\) forces \(x\in[0,1]\); also \(3x-1\in[-1,1]\Rightarrow x\le\tfrac23\).
Taking sine: \(3x-1=-\cos(2\sin^{-1}x)=2x^2-1\Rightarrow x=0\) or \(\tfrac32\). Only \(x=0\) works (both sides \(-\tfrac\pi2\)): \(1\) solution.

Let \(S=\{x\in[-\pi,\pi]:\sin x(\sin x+\cos x)=a,\ a\in\mathbb{Z}\}\). Then \(n(S)\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(\sin x(\sin x+\cos x)=\tfrac12+\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\sin\left(2x-\tfrac\pi4\right)\in\left[\tfrac12-\tfrac1{\sqrt2},\tfrac12+\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\right]\), so \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
\(a=0\): \(\sin x=0\) (\(x=-\pi,0,\pi\)) or \(\tan x=-1\) (\(x=-\tfrac\pi4,\tfrac{3\pi}{4}\)): \(5\) values.
\(a=1\): \(\cos x(\sin x-\cos x)=0\): \(x=\pm\tfrac\pi2\) or \(\tan x=1\) (\(x=\tfrac\pi4,-\tfrac{3\pi}4\)): \(4\) values. Total \(9\).

questions.q: Let \(P=\{\theta\in[0,4\pi]:\tan^2\theta\ne1\}\) and \(S=\{a\in\mathbb{Z}:2(\cos^8\theta-\sin^8\theta)\sec2\theta=a^2,\ \theta\in P\}\). Then \(n(S)\) is:
questions.sol:
\(\cos^8\theta-\sin^8\theta=(\cos^4\theta+\sin^4\theta)\cos2\theta\), so the expression is \(2(\cos^4\theta+\sin^4\theta)=2-\sin^22\theta\).
\(\tan^2\theta\ne1\Rightarrow\sin^22\theta\ne1\), so the value lies in \((1,2]\). No perfect square lies in \((1,2]\): \(n(S)=0\).

questions.q: If \(A=\dfrac{\sin3^\circ}{\cos9^\circ}+\dfrac{\sin9^\circ}{\cos27^\circ}+\dfrac{\sin27^\circ}{\cos81^\circ}\) and \(B=\tan81^\circ-\tan3^\circ\), then \(\dfrac BA\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
\(\tan3x-\tan x=\dfrac{\sin2x}{\cos3x\cos x}=\dfrac{2\sin x}{\cos3x}\), so \(\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos3x}=\tfrac12(\tan3x-\tan x)\).
\(A=\tfrac12(\tan81^\circ-\tan3^\circ)=\tfrac B2\), hence \(\tfrac BA=2\).

questions.q: Let \(\vec a_k=(\tan\theta_k)\hat i+\hat j\) and \(\vec b_k=\hat i-(\cot\theta_k)\hat j\), where \(\theta_k=\dfrac{2^{k-1}\pi}{2^n+1}\), for some \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), \(n>5\). Then the value of \(\dfrac{\sum_{k=1}^n|\vec a_k|^2}{\sum_{k=1}^n|\vec b_k|^2}\) is ______.
questions.sol:
\(|\vec a_k|^2=\sec^2\theta_k\), \(|\vec b_k|^2=\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta_k\). Since \(\dfrac{4}{\sin^22\theta}=\sec^2\theta+\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta\): \(\sec^2\theta_k=4\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta_{k+1}-\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta_k\).
Summing: \(\sum\sec^2\theta_k=3\sum_{k=1}^n\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta_k+4\left(\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta_{n+1}-\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta_1\right)\).
\(\theta_{n+1}=\pi-\theta_1\), so the bracket vanishes. Ratio \(=3\).

questions.q: Let \(\tan A,\tan B\), where \(A,B\in\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\), be the roots of the quadratic equation \(x^2-2x-5=0\). Then \(20\sin^2\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right)\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(\tan(A+B)=\dfrac{2}{1+5}=\dfrac13\). The roots have opposite signs, so \(A+B\in\left(-\tfrac\pi2,\tfrac\pi2\right)\), hence \(\cos(A+B)=\tfrac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\).
\(20\sin^2\tfrac{A+B}{2}=10(1-\cos(A+B))=10-3\sqrt{10}\).

questions.sol:

Sum of the integers from \(-15\) to \(9\): \(\dfrac{25(-15+9)}{2}=-75\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha=3+4+8+9+13+14+\dots\) up to \(40\) terms. If \((\tan\beta)^{\frac{\alpha}{1020}}\) is a root of the equation \(x^2+x-2=0\), \(\beta\in\left(0,\dfrac\pi2\right)\), then \(\sin^2\beta+3\cos^2\beta\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Pairing terms: \((3+4)+(8+9)+\dots=\sum_{k=0}^{19}(10k+7)=1900+140=2040\), so \(\tfrac{\alpha}{1020}=2\).
\(\tan^2\beta\) is a root of \(x^2+x-2=0\) and is non-negative, so \(\tan^2\beta=1\), \(\beta=\tfrac\pi4\).
\(\sin^2\beta+3\cos^2\beta=\tfrac12+\tfrac32=2\).

questions.q:
Let \(\alpha=3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac6{11}\right)\) and \(\beta=3\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac49\right)\), where inverse trigonometric functions take only the principal values. Given below are two statements:
Statement I: \(\cos(\alpha+\beta)>0\).
Statement II: \(\cos(\alpha)<0\).
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
\(\tfrac12<\tfrac6{11}<\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\Rightarrow\sin^{-1}\tfrac6{11}\in\left(\tfrac\pi6,\tfrac\pi4\right)\Rightarrow\alpha\in\left(\tfrac\pi2,\tfrac{3\pi}4\right)\), so \(\cos\alpha<0\): II true.
\(0<\tfrac49<\tfrac12\Rightarrow\cos^{-1}\tfrac49\in\left(\tfrac\pi3,\tfrac\pi2\right)\Rightarrow\beta\in\left(\pi,\tfrac{3\pi}2\right)\).
\(\alpha+\beta\in\left(\tfrac{3\pi}2,\tfrac{9\pi}4\right)\subset\left(\tfrac{3\pi}2,\tfrac{5\pi}2\right)\), where cosine is positive: I true.
